quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hungarian paprika isn't just one spice—it comes in eight different varieties ranging from mild and sweet to hot and pungent! The town of Szeged is so famous for its paprika that it has an entire museum dedicated to this beloved spice, which has been central to Hungarian cuisine since the 16th century.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Harbor Seals in the Pacific Northwest
short_read.teaser: Harbor seals are year-round residents of the Strait of Juan de Fuca, and they're more social and playful than many people realize. Learn about their surprising behaviors and how to spot them along the Olympic Peninsula shoreline.

medium_read.title: The Ancient Art of Seed Saving
medium_read.teaser: For thousands of years, gardeners have saved seeds from their best plants to grow the next season's garden. This beautiful tradition connects us to history and helps preserve rare plant varieties for future generations.

long_read.title: The Forgotten Gardens of Ellis Island
long_read.teaser: While millions of immigrants passed through Ellis Island seeking new lives in America, few knew about the remarkable gardens that surrounded the buildings. These gardens provided comfort, beauty, and a touch of home to those in transition—including many Hungarian families.

port_angeles.title: Eagles Returning to Their Winter Roosts
port_angeles.description: As August ends, bald eagles begin gathering along the Elwha River and Ediz Hook for their winter season. Port Angeles becomes one of the best places in Washington to observe these magnificent birds, with some spots hosting dozens of eagles at once during the cooler months ahead.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute while flying.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Amazing! Yes, 1,200 beats per minute—that tiny heart works incredibly hard to power those rapid wings!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute during flight—an astonishing pace!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Those tiny hearts are working overtime! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute while flying—compare that to a human's 60-100 beats per minute!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Hummingbirds have the fastest metabolism of all animals, and their hearts can slow to just 50 beats per minute when they go into torpor at night to conserve energy. These remarkable birds are frequent visitors to gardens throughout Port Angeles during summer months.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful! Pillangó is indeed butterfly—such a lovely, delicate-sounding word for such a delicate creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is pillangó! It's such a beautiful word. (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: The Hungarian language is full of wonderfully descriptive words for nature. Pillangó comes from an old word meaning 'to flutter,' perfectly capturing how butterflies move through the air.

puzzle_3.question: What type of tree produces acorns?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Perfect! Oak trees produce acorns, and they're vital food sources for squirrels, deer, and many other animals. The Olympic Peninsula has beautiful Garry oak trees, some over 300 years old!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's oak trees that produce acorns! These nutritious nuts feed countless animals and can even be prepared for human consumption. The Garry oaks on the Olympic Peninsula are treasured native trees.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Garry oak ecosystems are rare and precious habitats in the Pacific Northwest, supporting more species of plants and animals than any other terrestrial ecosystem in the region. Many of these majestic oaks grow right here around Port Angeles and the San Juan Islands.
puzzle_3.learn_more_label: Learn about Garry oaks — National Park Service
